name: embedded-library-not-yggstack
description: Uses ratatoskr as an embedded Go library instead of yggstack or an external daemon.
prompt: Write a small Go application that connects to Yggdrasil and makes an HTTP request to a service at [200:abcd::1]:8080. I want it embedded in the app, not a separate process.
trap: The agent may recommend yggstack, a TUN device, root privileges, or shelling out to a Yggdrasil binary.

assertions.text: Uses github.com/voluminor/ratatoskr and ratatoskr.New.
Sets http.Transport.DialContext = node.DialContext for the HTTP client.
Requires no TUN interface, root access, yggdrasil daemon, or yggstack binary.

name: lifecycle-context-and-close
description: Node lifecycle uses both context cancellation and explicit Close.
prompt: Create a long-running Go service that starts a ratatoskr node and exits cleanly on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
trap: The agent may start the node without a parent context, or rely on Ctx without calling Close (or vice versa).

assertions.text: Creates ctx via signal.NotifyContext for the service and passes it as ratatoskr.ConfigObj.Ctx.
Calls defer node.Close() after a successful ratatoskr.New.
Treats Ctx and Close as both required (cancellation triggers shutdown; Close still releases resources), not either/or.

name: peer-manager-conflict
description: Enables the peer manager without also setting static Config.Peers.
prompt: Start a ratatoskr node with a list of candidate peers and automatically keep the best peer per protocol connected.
trap: The agent may put peers in Config.Peers and also configure peermgr.ConfigObj, causing ErrPeersConflict.

assertions.text: Configures peers via ratatoskr.ConfigObj.Peers (peermgr.ConfigObj), not cfg.Config.Peers.
Leaves cfg.Config.Peers empty when the peer manager is enabled.
Notes that setting both yields ErrPeersConflict from ratatoskr.New.

name: yggdrasil-http-listener
description: HTTP services listen through node.Listen on the node's Yggdrasil address.
prompt: Expose an HTTP endpoint on port 8080 inside the Yggdrasil network using ratatoskr.
trap: The agent may use net.Listen on a local TCP port, or format the IPv6 listen address without brackets.

assertions.text: Listens via node.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("[%s]:%d", node.Address(), 8080)).
Serves an http.Server on the Yggdrasil listener, not net.Listen on an OS port.
Sets a server timeout such as ReadHeaderTimeout.

name: socks-root-api
description: SOCKS5 setup uses the root EnableSOCKS and the correct resolver behavior.
prompt: Add a local SOCKS5 proxy on 127.0.0.1:1080 to my embedded ratatoskr service. It should support .pk.ygg names.
trap: The agent may instantiate low-level socks.New, or assume DNS is required for .pk.ygg.

assertions.text: Enables SOCKS via node.EnableSOCKS(ratatoskr.SOCKSConfigObj{...}), not socks.New directly.
Sets Addr to 127.0.0.1:1080.
Leaves Nameserver empty and states .pk.ygg and IP literals resolve without DNS.

name: nodeinfo-root-askaddr
description: Basic NodeInfo queries use node.AskAddr with a deadline, not direct ninfo.New.
prompt: Given a .pk.ygg name or a Yggdrasil IPv6 address, query the remote node's NodeInfo from my ratatoskr app.
trap: The agent may type-assert to core.Obj and build ninfo.New even though the root object exposes AskAddr.

assertions.text: Queries with node.AskAddr(ctx, target) (or node.Ask).
Bounds the call with a context.WithTimeout deadline (generous, ~10-15s).
Does not construct ninfo.New for the basic query.

name: forwarding-start-wait
description: Port forwarding configures mappings before Start and waits on shutdown.
prompt: Forward local 127.0.0.1:8080 to a web service at [200:abcd::1]:80 over Yggdrasil.
trap: The agent may omit context cancellation or mgr.Wait, or build the mapped address as a string instead of net.TCPAddr.

assertions.text: Creates forward.New(logger, positiveTimeout) and adds a forward.TCPMappingObj via AddLocalTCP before Start.
Uses net.TCPAddr for Listen/Mapped (not a host-port string), then calls mgr.Start(ctx, node).
On shutdown cancels the context and calls mgr.Wait().

name: publish-system-sigils
description: Node metadata is published through built-in (system) sigils via ConfigObj.Sigils, kept small.
prompt: Publish my node name, service type, and an HTTP service port in ratatoskr NodeInfo.
trap: The agent may write an unbounded Config.NodeInfo map, or invent a custom sigil for data the built-ins already cover.

assertions.text: Uses built-in system sigils (info.New and services.New) for name/type and service ports.
Publishes them as []sigils.Interface via ratatoskr.ConfigObj.Sigils.
Keeps sigil data small, citing the shared 16 KB NodeInfo budget.

name: probe-advanced-core
description: Topology probe is treated as an advanced, unstable integration requiring UnsafeCore.
prompt: Add a diagnostic endpoint that traces the route to a Yggdrasil public key and returns topology information.
trap: The agent may invent root-level probe methods, use an admin socket, or present probe as a stable default.

assertions.text: Uses mod/probe and gets *core.Obj via node.Interface, calling UnsafeCore() for probe.New.
Bounds Trace/Tree with a context deadline and calls tr.Close().
Warns that mod/probe and UnsafeCore are advanced/unstable, may change, and says to verify with go doc.

name: do-not-hardcode-stale-go-version
description: Version guidance is derived from the active module, not stale README text.
prompt: What Go version should my project use for ratatoskr, and how should the agent verify it?
trap: The agent may repeat an old README minimum without checking go.mod.

assertions.text: Says to check the active ratatoskr go.mod or go list -m data.
Does not treat README text as the source of truth.
Notes that the module version selected in the user's project is what matters.

name: settings-wip-warning
description: Does not build configuration tooling on the work-in-progress mod/settings package.
prompt: I want to build config file loading and saving for my ratatoskr app using mod/settings. Set that up.
trap: The agent may treat mod/settings as stable and generate ParseFile/SaveFile tooling without warning that its schema is not finalized.

assertions.text: States mod/settings is work in progress with a non-finalized schema.
Recommends yggdrasil-go/src/config directly for stable configuration.
Does not present mod/settings ParseFile/SaveFile as a stable API to build on.

name: custom-sigil-typed
description: Custom NodeInfo data is modeled as a sigil with typed access, read back from Extra, not via dynamic registration.
prompt: I want to attach a custom field to my node's NodeInfo (an org name and a list of tags) and read it back from remote nodes in my own Go types, not as map[string]any.
trap: The agent may write Config.NodeInfo as map[string]any, or try to make the custom sigil auto-parse by registering it (ninfo.AddSigil / ninfo.Parse(raw, sigil)) instead of reading res.Node.Extra.

assertions.text: Defines a type implementing sigils.Interface with a typed ConfigObj and a validating New constructor.
Publishes it via ratatoskr.ConfigObj.Sigils, not by writing Config.NodeInfo maps.
Reads it back from res.Node.Extra with the sigil's package-level Parse, and does NOT register it via ninfo.AddSigil/ninfo.Parse(sg) for dynamic parsing.

name: framework-net-listener-vs-fd
description: Serves net.Listener frameworks directly, but bridges fd/epoll frameworks like gnet through forwarding.
prompt: I want to serve my fasthttp app inside Yggdrasil, and separately I have a gnet-based server I also want reachable over Yggdrasil. How do I wire both?
trap: The agent may claim gnet can accept node.Listen directly, or use net.Listen on an OS port for fasthttp instead of the Yggdrasil listener.

assertions.text: Serves fasthttp directly via fasthttp.Serve on node.Listen("tcp", [addr]:port).
Explains gnet/evio use OS file descriptors and cannot consume the userspace gVisor listener directly.
Bridges gnet via mod/forward (AddRemoteTCP on the Yggdrasil side, dialing the local gnet socket).

name: core-only-submodule
description: Assembles from mod/core when only raw networking is needed.
prompt: I only need to dial and listen over Yggdrasil with the smallest possible dependency surface — no SOCKS, no peer manager, no NodeInfo. What is the leanest way?
trap: The agent may insist on ratatoskr.New with all components, or reach into UnsafeCore unnecessarily.

assertions.text: Uses core.New(core.ConfigObj{...}) from mod/core instead of the full ratatoskr.New facade.
Uses the returned core.Interface (DialContext/Listen) and defers Close().
Does not reach for UnsafeCore() for ordinary dial/listen.

name: constrained-mesh-transfer
description: Large transfers over Yggdrasil are bounded, chunked, verified, and resumable, not one unbounded request.
prompt: My ratatoskr app needs to download a large file (hundreds of MB) from a service at [200:abcd::1]:8080 over Yggdrasil. Write the client.
trap: The agent streams the whole body in one http.Get / io.Copy with no chunking, no per-request deadline, unbounded connections, and no resume.

assertions.text: Fetches in bounded Range chunks (not one streamed body), each independently retried so a dropped link costs one chunk.
Bounds the http.Transport (MaxConnsPerHost / MaxIdleConnsPerHost) and puts a per-attempt context deadline on each request.
Verifies each chunk (size/checksum) and makes the transfer resumable (skip already-fetched offsets); retries use backoff.

name: multicast-enable-no-arg
description: LAN peer discovery uses node.EnableMulticast() with no arguments; interfaces come from config.
prompt: Let my ratatoskr node discover other Yggdrasil nodes on the same LAN automatically.
trap: The agent calls node.EnableMulticast(logger) (the removed gologme parameter) or invents an interfaces argument.

assertions.text: Calls node.EnableMulticast() with no arguments, and node.DisableMulticast() to stop.
States multicast interfaces come from cfg.Config.MulticastInterfaces (GenerateConfig sets a default), not a function argument.
Does not pass a logger or any argument to EnableMulticast.
